evidence.quote: In a statement , the Singapore Police Force (SPF) said that it had issued a “prohibition of disposal order” against a residence valued at around S$55 million ($42.4 million) and seized around S$1 million of funds in connection with fraud investigations.
evidence.one_line: The Singapore Police Force said it issued a prohibition-of-disposal order against a residence valued at around S$55 million ($42.4 million) and seized around S$1 million in funds in connection with fraud investigations.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, as quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: The investigation centers on two Singaporeans, Aaron Woon and Alan Wei, who were charged in February 2025 with criminal conspiracy to commit fraud, and a Chinese national named Li Ming, who was charged at the same time with committing fraud by false representation.
evidence.one_line: Aaron Woon and Alan Wei were charged with criminal conspiracy to commit fraud, and Li Ming was charged with fraud by false representation, in February 2025.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Singaporean authorities, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: In April of this year, a fourth defendant, Jenny Lim, was charged in connection with the case.
evidence.one_line: Jenny Lim was charged in connection with the case in April 2026.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Singaporean authorities, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: At the time of the alleged offences, Woon, Wei, and Lim were key officers of three companies, Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, and Aperia Cloud Services – collectively known as the Aperia Group – that are alleged to have concealed the actual end-user of servers.
evidence.one_line: Authorities allege that Aperia International, A-Speed Infotech, and Aperia Cloud Services, through officers Woon, Wei, and Lim, concealed the actual end-user of servers.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Singaporean authorities, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Separately, Li was found through investigations to be the controller of another company, Luxuriate Your Life, that was allegedly involved in the scheme.
evidence.one_line: Investigators identified Li Ming as the controller of Luxuriate Your Life, which was allegedly involved in the scheme.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Investigators, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Authorities say that the servers in question, which may have contained advanced Nvidia AI chips, were shipped from Singapore to Malaysia .
evidence.one_line: Authorities said servers that may have contained advanced Nvidia AI chips were shipped from Singapore to Malaysia.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Singaporean authorities, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Yesterday, police also announced additional charges of fraud and money laundering against the defendants. Lim and Woon were each handed seven new charges, while Wei is set to receive seven new charges on July 6, the SPF said.
evidence.one_line: On July 1, 2026, police announced seven new charges each against Lim and Woon, and said Wei was set to receive seven new charges on July 6, 2026.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, as quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: The fraud charges allege that the three “engaged in a conspiracy to commit fraud in respect of the purchase of servers” from the U.S. companies Dell, Super Micro Computer, and Asus.
evidence.one_line: The charges allege that Lim, Woon, and Wei conspired to commit fraud over server purchases from Dell, Super Micro Computer, and Asus.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, as quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: The charges assert that between November 2023 and February 2025, the trio “falsely represented, in communications to these suppliers, that one of the Aperia Group companies would be the end-user of the servers.”
evidence.one_line: The charges allege that from November 2023 through February 2025, the three defendants falsely represented to suppliers that an Aperia Group company would be the servers’ end-user.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, as quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: The four companies will also face a total of eight charges of fraud by false representation which are due to be announced on July 6, which the SPF said was “the first instance of corporate entities being prosecuted in relation to these investigations.”
evidence.one_line: The SPF said four companies would face a total of eight fraud-by-false-representation charges, due to be announced July 6, 2026, describing it as the first prosecution of corporate entities in these investigations.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, as quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Lim and Woon were also charged with money laundering, after “each acquiring approximately SG$1.2 million in their personal bank accounts,” which pointed to benefits from criminal conduct, police said.
evidence.one_line: Police said Lim and Woon were charged with money laundering after each acquired approximately S$1.2 million in personal bank accounts, which police said pointed to criminal proceeds.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, as quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Wei faces three counts of money laundering relating to the aforementioned seized mansion, and an additional S$5.8 that was deposited in his personal account, and which police allege was partly made up of benefits from criminal conduct.
evidence.one_line: Wei faces three money-laundering counts relating to the seized mansion and an additional S$5.8 deposited in his personal account, which police allege was partly criminal proceeds.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Singapore Police Force, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: In addition to this, Li was also slapped with additional charges of fraud related to a similar misrepresentation of the end-user of servers that Luxuriate Your Life intended to purchase from the U.S. firm Super Micro.
evidence.one_line: Li Ming faced additional fraud charges alleging misrepresentation of the end-user for servers Luxuriate Your Life intended to buy from Super Micro.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Singaporean authorities, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: In February of last year, the same month that saw the initial arrests in this chip-smuggling case, it was reported that the U.S. Commerce Department was initiating investigations into whether the Chinese AI company DeepSeek had gained access to restricted Nvidia chips, and whether these chips had been sourced from third parties in countries including Malaysia and Singapore .
evidence.one_line: In February 2025, reports said the U.S. Commerce Department was investigating whether DeepSeek obtained restricted Nvidia chips through third parties in countries including Malaysia and Singapore.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Unspecified reports cited by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Singapore said that it is unaware of any smuggling taking place in the country, but that it would come down hard on any individuals or entities found to be breaching the law – a stance that the SPF reiterated in yesterday’s statement.
evidence.one_line: Singapore said it was unaware of smuggling in the country and would act firmly against individuals or entities found to breach the law.
evidence.speaker: Singaporean authorities, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: “The police hold a zero-tolerance stance towards such offenses and will act resolutely against those, whether businesses or individuals, who violate our laws, and safeguard Singapore’s integrity as a trusted global financial and business hub underpinned by the rule of law,” the statement read.
evidence.one_line: The Singapore Police Force said it would act resolutely against businesses or individuals violating Singaporean law.
evidence.speaker: Singapore Police Force, quoted by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: Last week, Malaysian authorities said they had foiled an attempt to smuggle advanced AI chips through the country’s main airport, seizing 72 servers worth nearly $13 million.
evidence.one_line: Malaysian authorities said they foiled an attempt to smuggle advanced AI chips through the country’s main airport and seized 72 servers worth nearly $13 million in late June 2026.
evidence.speaker: Malaysian authorities, as reported by The Diplomat

evidence.quote: The U.S. government is probing whether the Hangzhou-based AI firm has built its disruptive R1 AI model on restricted Nvidia chips.
evidence.one_line: The U.S. government is probing whether DeepSeek built its R1 model using restricted Nvidia chips.
evidence.speaker: The Diplomat
evidence.original_who: Unspecified source; the item does not identify the origin of this claim

evidence.quote: The number of such cases more than tripled from 589 in the first half of 2024 to 1,762 over the same period this year, according to the Singaporean police.
evidence.one_line: Singapore police reported 1,762 such cases in the first half of 2026, up from 589 in the first half of 2024, a more-than-threefold increase.
evidence.speaker: Singaporean police, as reported by The Diplomat
evidence.event_time: First half of 2024 and first half of 2026
